_comment: ngsolve stokes#2 (enclosed-flow Stokes has a constant-pressure nullspace; open flows do not; the singular system stays quiet). Run 2026-08-06 on NGSolve 6.2.2604 on one mesh (unit square maxh 0.25, Taylor-Hood order 2/1) with two boundary conditions that differ ONLY in whether the right edge is traction-free. The enclosed system has exactly one singular value at 4.3e-16 against a next of 6.2e-4; its right singular vector puts 100% of its norm in the pressure block with a relative spread of 3.7e-14, so it is the constant-pressure mode. The open system has no zero singular value at all -- smallest 6.3e-4 -- confirming the claim's second sentence. Solving the singular system raises nothing, prints nothing (checked at the file-descriptor level) and returns a finite vector. Both fixes the claim names are exercised: pinning one pressure DOF and a NumberSpace mean-zero multiplier give velocities agreeing to 1.3e-17, and the NumberSpace route additionally drives the pressure mean to 5.2e-18 while pinning leaves it at 0.5 -- so the two are not interchangeable if the pressure's constant matters. Mutation: giving the 'open' problem full Dirichlet velocity BCs makes it singular too and the fixture fails on open_flow_pressure_is_unique. MUTATION CONTROL (re-runnable): T2_MUTATE=1 changes the dirichlet string build() receives for the OPEN problem from 'bot|top|left' to '.*', closing the traction-free right edge so that problem acquires the same constant-pressure nullspace as the enclosed one. Re-verified by execution 2026-08-06 on NGSolve 6.2.2604: the unmutated run matches all 8 expect_in_output strings; T2_MUTATE=1 removes 'open_flow_pressure_is_unique=True' and makes the forbidden 'FAIL:' appear, so the fixture goes red. Re-run: T2_MUTATE=1 python source.py
